beginner: Try not to feed it. Sage needs very little, and too much fertilizer gives floppy growth and weaker-tasting leaves. The same is true for water, where more is not better.
seasoned: Resist the urge to feed. Sage has low fertility needs, and over-feeding gives soft growth with weaker flavor. The same goes for water: more is not better.

beginner: Trim sage back in spring when new growth starts. Cut the leggy stems but not down into the hard old wood, which does not grow back well. This yearly trim keeps it bushy and slows it going woody, but you will still replace plants every few years.

seasoned: Spring into early summer is the best harvest window. Cut sprigs freely from new growth, taking no more than about half the plant, and harvest in mid-morning after the dew dries for the strongest flavor.
